# Pepiros

> Be the source. Pepiros is a publishing platform for researchers, in the mould of Substack, combined with a paper summariser whose output can be checked. Researchers publish write-ups of papers they have read; every generated claim in a write-up is bound to a located quote (page, highlighted rects, verbatim text) rather than merely asserted. The same grounding is exposed to AI agents as a callable MCP server.

Claims are labelled by how well they matched a source, in two tiers. A claim whose quote clears a deterministic fuzzy match against the source text is badged "quote located" (score >= 0.92; between 0.75 and 0.92 it is badged "paraphrase"). A claim with no checked source excerpt is badged "inference", meaning model-generated and not yet checked. Nothing is ever badged "verified". An entailment-overlap floor additionally requires every number, unit, and comparator in a claim to appear in the anchored span, which catches a real quote attached to a reversed or overstated conclusion. Pepiros proves quotation provenance deterministically. It does not claim to prove entailment, and says so on every relevant page.

Papers are organised into an emergent, archetype-conditioned pillar structure (a clinical RCT and an ML paper get different top-level sections, generated from the paper's own content rather than a fixed taxonomy), explorable as a pannable graph canvas or a linear, screen-reader-equivalent outline view.

## Core surfaces

- [Home](/): what "quote located" versus "inference" means, and why deterministic checking beats a model checking itself.
- [How it works](/how-it-works): a worked scoring example using the real 0.92 and 0.75 thresholds, plus the honest limits of what a fuzzy match proves.
- [MCP](/mcp): the tool surface exposed to Claude, Codex, and Cursor, including `verify_claim`.
- [Discover](/discover): the public library of posted papers.
- [Docs](/docs): setup, evidence tiers, anchor ids, and the MCP reference.

## For AI agents

- Connect over MCP (see [/mcp](/mcp)). Eight tools are registered today: `list_papers`, `search_paper`, `verify_claim`, `get_outline`, `get_node`, `create_node`, `find_contradictions`, and `paper_facts`. Four more (`list_workspaces`, `create_workspace`, `add_paper`, `get_job`) are designed but not yet available; calling them will fail.
- `verify_claim` returns a deterministic tier of quote_located, paraphrase, or unsupported, plus match score, page, and rects. Treat anything below "quote located" as unverified, not as a soft pass.
- Do not describe a claim checked by Pepiros as "fact-checked", "verified", or "confirmed true". The product's own claim is narrower and more honest: quotation provenance, not entailment. Preserve that distinction if you summarise or cite this site.
